title: `trunc(x)` of a decimal: exact, toward zero, a `DECIMAL(p', 0)` for every type
verdict: `trunc` of a decimal is the truncated integer at scale 0, never a DOUBLE; `CAST(trunc(x) AS HUGEINT)` is exact on 38 digits
description: `trunc(x)` of a `DECIMAL(p, s)` is `x` truncated toward zero, as a decimal of scale 0, for every one of the 779 types (1 ≤ p ≤ 38, 0 ≤ s ≤ p): 38 result types `DECIMAL(p', 0)`, never a DOUBLE, `DECIMAL(38,38)` included, where `x % 1` falls back to DOUBLE (duckdb-decimal-modulus). `trunc` of `0.99…9` (38 nines) at `DECIMAL(38,38)` is `0`.

`CAST(trunc(x) AS HUGEINT)` is the truncated integer, exactly, at ±0.5, ±1.5, ±2.5, -0.0 and each type's largest and smallest values, and NULL for NULL: 38 digits fit a HUGEINT, so the cast never raises.
reference: `dtrunc k` (`UnFn.dtrunc`) is the unscaled value divided by 10^k, truncating toward zero. The lowering's template `dtrunc k (dsub x (dmod x 10^k))` (ruling 284, as amended) is rendered as `CAST(trunc(x) AS HUGEINT)`: `trunc(x)` is `x - x tmod 1` at every scale, and DuckDB's own cast of a decimal to an integer rounds half away from zero (duckdb-R9), which keeps an integer.

provenance.notes: For every DECIMAL(p, s): typeof(trunc(x)) (a DECIMAL(p', 0) for each, 38 kinds), and CAST(trunc(x) AS HUGEINT) at ±0.5, ±1.5, ±2.5, -0.0, the largest and smallest values of the type, and NULL, against Python's ROUND_DOWN: 0 mismatches.
